text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's state-owned telecoms monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) will increase service prices by 11 percent this year, while the post office Poczta Polska will increase its prices by 13 percent in February, the companies said.

- Sweden's Lion Queen shipping firm transported 141,000 passengers, 23,000 passenger cars and 9,000 trucks between Poland and Sweden in 1996, showing significant growth over 1995. It plans to introduce another ferry on routes between the two countries soon, the company said.
- Poland's per capita juice consumption in 1996 was 11 litres and will keep growing by 20 percent annually for the next two years, a forecast by the Tymbark juice producer said.
NOWA EUROPA

- The opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) criticised the 1997 budget bill for incoherence and a tendency for politicised distribution of funds in an election year, UW chief Leszek Balcerowicz said.
- The Jawor sugar mill in Jaworzyna, southwestern Poland, has received a kosher certificate which will facilitate sugar exports to Israel, marketing director Kazimierz Pokora said.
- It would have been possible to push Poland's inflation below 18.5 percent last year but this would have held back economic growth, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- As a result of Bank Handlowy's (BH) privatisation the bank should gain the support of institutional investors, which will provide stability and enhance management through transfer of know-how and technology, BH President Cezary Stypulkowaski said.
- Creditanstalt Poland bank has increased its stake in the listed Mostostal Warszawa construction firm to 13.3 percent, the bank said.
- The net profit of the listed Optimus computer firm in 1996 was 16.5 million zlotys, its preliminary report said.
ZYCIE
- Israel's Dankner group plans to invest in petrol distribution in Poland and Belarus together with the Polish state-owned CPN petrol producer and distributor, Dankner said.
- Around 2,000 workers of the Gdynia shipyard went on strike yesterday and picketted the management offices to demand overdue salaries and a pay rise.
- Poland's budget deficit in 1996 was 9.122 billion zlotys, the finance ministry said.
PARKIET

- The total net losses of Poland's National Investment Funds (NFI) were 500 million zlotys, but much of this total arose from new auditing practices introduced under the September 1994 audits act, the treasury ministry's NFI department director Roman Galimski said.

- The listed Budimex construction firm's sales will increase by 56.8 percent in 1996, while sales by the company's capital group will increase by 44.9 percent, the company said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
